# @k8ordo/framework

> Turns `src/routes/` into an application of React Server Components, built
> with Vite, in one of two modes chosen in `vite.config.ts`:
> `framework({ mode: 'static', site })` renders every route at build time into
> files a static host serves, with no server, and
> `framework({ mode: 'server' })` renders per request on a server. Switching
> takes more than `mode`: towards server, drop `site` and `csp` (refused
> there; the policy becomes a header a `guard.ts` writes) and run
> `dist/server.js` or hand the handler to a host; towards static, add
> `site`, give every parameter's directory a `paths.ts` (or its page a
> `fallback.tsx`), and remove what static mode refuses and every read of the
> `request` prop — a layout's `nonce()` from `/server` included. The
> route grammar, the boundaries and the handler stay the same. Pick `server` when the application needs the request — Server
> Actions, `guard.ts`, the `request` prop, cookies, a page that exports
> `search`, parameter values with no list rendered on the server (static
> mode has only a `fallback.tsx`'s shell for those, drawn in the browser), a
> `[...name]` directory — and `static` otherwise; static mode refuses all of those by name, in the
> build and in `vite dev` (`this application wants mode: 'server'`).
> `src/routes/` is the pathname space and holds nothing else
> (page/layout/not-found/error/loading/fallback/paths/redirect/guard/route
> files,
> `[param]` and `(group)` directories, and under server mode `[...name]`,
> which takes every remaining segment — one or more — as an array
> (`/files/:path+`); `_` is an ordinary character in
> a segment and a name starting with `.` is not read, so `/.well-known` cannot
> be a route; components live outside it in `src/components/` and every
> other module in `src/lib/`); a page or layout may
> `export const paramsSchema` (any Standard Schema, synchronous) to type its
> parameters — a refused value makes the pattern not answer, so the walk goes
> on to `not-found.tsx` — a page that says `notFound()` is answered by the
> nearest `not-found.tsx`, an `error.tsx` shows in place of what throws below
> it, a `loading.tsx` shows while what is below it suspends, a `redirect.ts`
> answers 307/308 (server) or is written as a page that sends the visitor on
> (static), and a `route.ts` answers its URL with a `Response` (server: every
> method it exports; static: written as the file its `GET` answers). Under
> server mode a Server Action, a `guard.ts` and a `route.ts` end the request
> with `redirect(href(…))` (a `303` from a guard or a `route.ts`) or, the
> last two, `notFound()`, a `guard.ts` runs before whatever answers below it, `cookies()` reads and writes cookies, and a page
> receives `request`. Under static mode a parameter's values come from a
> `paths.ts` in its directory (a function returning them, typed `Paths`,
> run with the pages' own modules, applied to every route below it) —
> beside a `fallback.tsx`, the values it does not return get a shell: the
> layouts written as HTML, the page drawn in the browser from the URL, and a
> `_redirects` (or `vercel()`'s routes) through which a host reaches it —
> writes `404.html` and `sitemap.xml`, and puts a Content-Security-Policy in
> a `<meta>` by hash (`csp`). Application code imports from `@k8ordo/framework`
> (the router's `href`, `notFound`, `PageProps`, …); `@k8ordo/router` is a
> required peer but never named. Boundaries are React's own `'use client'`
> with `server-only` modules barred from the client bundle, and the route
> table and type wiring are generated rather than hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

When installed via npm, these docs live under `node_modules/@k8ordo/framework/docs/`.
Start with GUIDE.md, then follow the reference most relevant to the task.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](GUIDE.md): choosing a mode and what static mode refuses,
  setup (install, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, the root layout as the
  document), `vite dev` and `vite preview` against a static build, the
  browsers a build is aimed at (Baseline newly available, unless the config
  sets its own targets), the entries, the plugin's options —
  `reactCompiler` (React Compiler on the client components, which needs
  `oxc-transform-react` installed), `headers` on every answer, and
  static mode's `site` and `csp` — where a visitor's preference is kept
  (look-only: `defineLocalState` and `inlineRead()`; one the server answers
  by: `defineCookieState` under server mode; the language: a plain cookie
  passed to `negotiateRequest` as `chosen`) — and testing: what answers a request
  through the built handler or `serve({ port: 0 })`, since the request API
  throws outside a request.

## References

- [Routing](references/routing.md): the `routes/` grammar and every refusal
  the build names, rest parameters (`[...name]`, server mode only: the
  pattern `/files/:path+`, an array of decoded segments for the page, layout,
  `route.ts` and `guard.ts`, never zero segments, always the last directory,
  tried after a literal and a `[name]` beside it and before the
  `not-found.tsx`), where a `fallback.tsx` may sit, a layout's current link
  (`matchPath(pattern, pathname)` on the server, `useMatch` in a client) and
  the one way to write each URL (a table shared with `@k8ordo/router` and
  `@k8ordo/state`), how a page is sent in
  each mode (each page loads only its own client components and CSS, what
  every page loads comes in at most two files — the entry's and the frame's,
  which sets the client build's `codeSplitting` — and the browser renders
  once they have loaded; Server Components' stylesheets
  come before client components', a stylesheet once loaded stays, and an
  inline classic script in `<head>` is moved ahead of every stylesheet, so
  a script that has to run before the first paint goes there),
  `loading.tsx`, `route.ts` (methods and `405` under server
  mode, a file under static mode), the generated `.k8ordo/` files (the
  route table, and the `Register`s: the table's, and `@k8ordo/i18n`'s when
  `src/i18n.ts` exports `locales` by name) and `k8ordo generate`, which
  writes them before `tsc` without a build, titles,
  and fetching the next page ahead (`data-k8ordo-prefetch`; under static
  mode also the links on screen for a coarse pointer, every page kept for
  going back and forward, and `client-files.json` linked with a payload),
  MDX (the application's own compiler plugin, `enforce: 'pre'`; the CSS
  an `.mdx` file imports reaches the pages rendering it, with no query),
  and counting page views (`navigatesuccess`, not `usePathname()`).
- [Parameters](references/params.md): `paramsSchema` — a refused value is a
  pathname the pattern does not answer; a `[...name]` directory's receives
  the array of segments — and, under static mode, `paths.ts`:
  the values of its directory's parameter (`Paths<Pattern>`, typed as a
  link takes them, spelled as `href` spells them), given the params above
  it as the layouts above its directory read them (their `paramsSchema`
  exports; values one of them refuses fail the build), for every page,
  `route.ts` and `redirect.ts` below it,
  and what fails the build; and `fallback.tsx` for the values it does not
  return — the shell it renders (no props, the layouts' schemas only, the
  shell's `pathname`), where a shell stands (below the values of the
  `paths.ts` files above it, which a layout receiving a parameter forces to
  exist), reading the value in the browser with `useMatch`, `notFound()`
  shown in place, routes below its parameter, what it costs, and how
  `vite dev` answers a value no `paths.ts` returns.
- [Errors and redirects](references/errors.md): `error.tsx` and reporting
  from it (what no `error.tsx` catches — the root layout's own components —
  and why there is no `global-error.tsx`), a Server Component that throws
  stopping a static build, `notFound()` and `not-found.tsx` (a document
  waits for its page under server mode; from a `guard.ts` or a `route.ts`,
  the same 404; under a `fallback.tsx`, shown in place), and `redirect.ts`
  in each mode — its `to` a pattern in the table's terms, where
  `redirect()` takes a URL.
- [Execution boundaries](references/boundaries.md): `'use client'`,
  `use(browser())` for a component that needs a browser (and `useMatch` /
  `usePathname` waiting for it on their own under a `fallback.tsx`),
  `server-only` modules, the search — `@k8ordo/state`'s, or handed to a
  page that exports `search` under server mode — and forms.
- [Server Actions](references/actions.md): server mode only. `'use server'`
  against `server-only`, `cookies()` / `responseHeaders()` /
  `requestHeaders()` / `waitUntil()` in an action, the page context an
  action runs in, forms before JavaScript, and ending with `redirect()`.
- [Guards, cookies and the request](references/guards.md): server mode only.
  `guard.ts` (outer first; `redirect(href(…))` ends the request with a
  `303`, `notFound()` with the nearest `not-found.tsx` under 404, a returned
  `Response` — a `401` — as it is),
  `responseHeaders()`, `cookies()` and its defaults, `waitUntil(promise)`
  for work that goes on after the answer (what it means, where it may be
  called, a rejection logged once), and the read-only `request` a page
  receives.
- [Content Security Policy](references/csp.md): `nonce()` in a header a
  guard writes under server mode, in `style-src` too for the framework's
  one `<style>`; the `csp` option and `colorSchemeScriptHash()` under static
  mode, and `connect-src` for the data a `fallback.tsx`'s shell fetches; an
  application's own pre-paint script (`inlineRead()`) as a `'use client'`
  component taking the nonce, its text hashed for static mode.
- [Running and deploying](references/deploy.md): a static build's
  `dist/client/` (HTML, `index.rsc` payloads, shells, `404.html`,
  `client-files.json`, `sitemap.xml`, `_redirects`), the rewrites that reach a shell on Netlify,
  Cloudflare Workers static assets (`html_handling`, the 2,000/100 rule
  limits) and Pages, Vercel and any other host, and `serve` and
  `vite preview` serving a static build as a static host; `headers`, the
  headers every response carries in either mode (`vite dev`,
  `vite preview`, `serve`, the handler, Vercel's routes, `_headers`);
  under server mode, a `dist/` that runs on its own with
  `node dist/server.js` (`PORT`, `HOST`, every dependency bundled in, and
  `resolve.external` for one that cannot be), `serve` (compression, `ETag`,
  `Range`, `close()` waiting for what `waitUntil()` was handed), the request
  handler under Node.js, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers and the
  `HandlerContext` it takes as a second argument, the same-origin rule for a
  `POST`, and `vercel()` in either mode (under server mode its function's
  `maxDuration` and `regions`, and `@vercel/functions` installed for
  `waitUntil()`),
  with routes of your own under static mode;
  a tab opened before a deploy, and Vite's `base`.

## Entry points

- `@k8ordo/framework` — what application code imports, re-exported from
  `@k8ordo/router` (which stays a peer, one copy): `href`,
  `bindParams`, `notFound`, `isNotFound`, `usePathname`,
  `usePendingPathname`, `useMatch`, `matchPath`, `normalizePathname`,
  `withBase`, and the types `PageProps`, `LayoutProps`, `RouteContext`,
  `ErrorProps`, `BoundParams`, `MatchablePattern`,
  `MatchOptions` and the `Registered*` types; and two
  types of its own, `Paths<Pattern>`, what a `paths.ts` exports by default,
  and `RedirectTarget`, what a `redirect.ts` does.
  Not `useParams` or `useRoute`: a page receives `params` as a prop.
- `@k8ordo/framework/vite` — `framework(options)` returns the Vite plugins;
  `options.mode` (`'static' | 'server'`) is required; the route files
  always live in `src/routes/`, and a key the mode does not take throws
  as the config loads. Only with
  `mode: 'static'`: `options.site`, required, the origin the site is
  served from (no path) — the origin of every request the build makes, a
  `route.ts`'s included, and of `sitemap.xml` — and
  `options.csp` (directives → sources, `ContentSecurityPolicy`) is the
  Content-Security-Policy written into each page's `<meta>`, first in
  `<head>` after the `<meta charSet>`, with the hashes of the framework's own inline scripts on that
  page added to `script-src` (or `default-src` made into it) and
  `script-src-elem`; a policy with `'strict-dynamic'`, `frame-ancestors`,
  `report-uri`, `report-to` or `sandbox` is refused. `FrameworkOptions` is
  `StaticOptions | ServerOptions`. This entry loads Vite and is for
  `vite.config.ts` only.
- `@k8ordo/framework/server` — server mode only; a static build refuses any
  module that imports a value from it. What code inside the request handler
  imports, needing nothing from Node but `AsyncLocalStorage`: `redirect(url)`
  ends what answers the request — a Server Action, a `guard.ts` or a
  `route.ts` (the last two with a `303`) — by sending the visitor to the URL
  `href()` built, and throws by name while a page renders; `responseHeaders()`
  is the `Headers` the final response carries, `cookies()` the request's
  cookies to read and write (`get`, `has`, `set(name, value,
  CookieOptions)`, `delete(name, CookieScope)`; defaults `path: '/'`,
  `httpOnly`, `secure` (not over plain HTTP to `localhost`),
  `sameSite: 'lax'`; every write a `Set-Cookie` on the answer), and
  `requestHeaders()` the headers the request arrived with — all three from
  a `guard.ts`, a `route.ts` or a Server Action, and they throw anywhere
  else; `nonce()` is the nonce this answer's inline scripts carry, new per
  request and readable anywhere the request is answered, the render
  included; `waitUntil(promise)` keeps the host from stopping until
  `promise` settles, for work that goes on after the answer — callable
  anywhere the request is in progress, the render included, a rejection
  logged once and never left unhandled; `HandlerContext`
  (`{ waitUntil?: (promise: Promise<unknown>) => void }`) is the type of
  the second argument the built handler takes from a runtime that calls it;
  `Guard<P>` is the type of what a `guard.ts` default-exports
  (`({ request, params }) => Response | void`) and `GuardContext<P>` its
  argument; `RouteRequest` is the type of the `request` prop.
- `@k8ordo/framework/serve` — the Node.js server for a build.
  `serve({ dist?, port?, host? })` (`ServeOptions`: `dist` defaults to
  `dist` under the working directory, `port` to `3000`, `host` to
  `localhost`) serves a build and returns a `Server`, `{ port, url, close }`
  (`port: 0` takes a free port; `close()` resolves once the answers under
  way are written and what `waitUntil()` was handed has settled): for a
  server build, the client build's
  files as they are and everything else through the request handler; for a
  static build, as a static host does — files, the `_redirects` rewrites,
  `404.html` under 404, never the handler. `dist/server.js` runs it under
  server mode; a server of your own imports it, with `@k8ordo/framework` in
  `dependencies`.
- `dist/server.js` — under server mode, what the build writes to start
  `serve` on the build it sits in: `node dist/server.js`, listening on
  `PORT` (default `3000`) and `HOST` (default `localhost`), closing —
  after the work handed to `waitUntil()` — and exiting with `0` on `SIGTERM`
  or `SIGINT`. `serve` and every
  dependency of the handler are bundled into `dist/`, with
  `dist/package.json` (written in either mode) marking it ES modules, so
  `dist/` runs with nothing installed and the framework is a dev
  dependency.
- `dist/rsc/index.js` — under server mode, the built request handler, a
  `(request: Request, context?: HandlerContext) => Promise<Response>`
  default export (`context.waitUntil` is the host's own) with every
  dependency bundled in, that needs nothing from its runtime but
  `AsyncLocalStorage` (`node:async_hooks`), so Node.js, Bun, Deno and
  Cloudflare Workers with `nodejs_compat` run it directly; the host serves
  `dist/client/` in front of it.
- `@k8ordo/framework/vercel` — `vercel()` returns a Vite plugin to put
  beside `framework()`, in either mode: `vite build` then also writes
  `.vercel/output/` (Build Output API v3) for `vercel build` /
  `vercel deploy --prebuilt` — the client build as static files at Vite's
  `base` (`assets/` immutable), and under server mode the request handler
  as one streaming Node.js function; under static mode no function, the
  shells' rewrites as routes tried after the files, then `404.html`, and
  each file a `route.ts` wrote served with the `Content-Type` its `GET`
  answered (`overrides`) where other hosts go by its extension.
  Under static mode `vercel({ beforeFiles, beforeNotFound })` also takes
  routes of the application's own (`VercelRoute`: `src`, `dest`, `status`,
  `headers`, `continue`, `check`, `caseSensitive`, `has`), written as given
  before the files and before `404.html`; Vercel alone applies them,
  matching `src` against the whole pathname (`^/posts/.+$`, not
  `^/posts/`).
- `@k8ordo/framework/generated` — what the generated `.k8ordo/` files
  import (`defineRoutes`, `Register`, …). Not for code written by hand.
- `k8ordo generate` — the package's one command (its `bin`), run in the
  application's directory: resolves the Vite config there as `vite build`
  does and writes `.k8ordo/` as the build does when it begins, then stops —
  no environment built, no page rendered, no `paths.ts` read — so CI
  runs it before `tsc` without the data a build reads. A `routes/` with
  the problems the build names under
  `routes/ is not a valid pathname space:` fails it the same way (exit
  code 1), with nothing written. What `mode: 'static'` refuses on top of
  those — a `[...name]` directory, a `guard.ts`, a `route.ts` answering more than `GET`, a page
  reading `search`, an `export *`, a Server Action, whatever a `paths.ts`
  returns — it does not check, so its success is not the build's.
